title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E526 is Euler's late, systematic return to the transverse vibrations of elastic rods and laminae. He says he is redoing the topic accurately now that the principles of mechanics and the analysis of functions of two variables (PDEs) are better developed. Before treating motion he states two lemmas without proof, saying he has proved them elsewhere, including the non-planar case. Lemma I, on this page, gives the equilibrium of a planar rod with arbitrary distributed loads.

Setup:
- The rod EYF is referred to a fixed axis OV. A point Y has Cartesian coordinates x = OX, y = XY, and arclength s = EY measured from the end E, with ds^2 = dx^2 + dy^2.
- The element ds has mass S ds (S is the linear density; mass plays no role in statics).
- The absolute elasticity (flexural rigidity) V may vary with position.
- The elastic restoring moment is V/r, with r the radius of curvature. In Cartesian form with no differential held constant this is V(dy ddx - dx ddy)/ds^3, i.e. V times the signed curvature.
- All loads on the element are resolved into P ds along the x-direction (YP) and Q ds along the y-direction (YQ).

Equilibrium condition: ∫dy∫P ds - ∫dx∫Q ds = V(dy ddx - dx ddy)/ds^3.

Interpretation: the left side is the moment about Y of all forces on the portion EY.
- Write F_x(s) = ∫_0^s P ds' and F_y(s) = ∫_0^s Q ds' for the resultant loads on EY.
- The moment about Y is ∫_0^s [(y(s) - y(s'))P(s') - (x(s) - x(s'))Q(s')] ds'.
- Integrating by parts, the first term equals ∫_0^s F_x dy, and similarly for the second.
- So the left side is exactly Euler's ∫dy∫P ds - ∫dx∫Q ds.

Setting this moment equal to the elastic moment V·κ gives the exact, geometrically nonlinear elastica equation for variable stiffness and arbitrary distributed loads. Differentiating twice would give the familiar (Vκ)'' form when linearized.

The next page completes the lemma:
- the tangential tension -(dx/ds)∫P ds - (dy/ds)∫Q ds, i.e. the projection of the resultant on the tangent;
- the naturally curved case, where V/ρ is subtracted;
- a remark that concentrated end forces at E are included in the integrals.

Purpose: the static moment law is converted in Lemma 2 into equations of motion by d'Alembert's principle (P, Q replaced by P - S d²x/dt², etc.). This yields the partial differential equations for rod vibrations treated in the rest of the paper.
errors: No mathematical error. The sign of the curvature expression (dy ddx - dx ddy)/ds^3 is a convention and must match the orientation of the moment. Integration constants (end loads and moments) are absorbed into the integrals, as Euler notes on the next page. The statement is given without proof, by Euler's own admission.

ideas.what: Moment balance of the portion EY: bending moment equals flexural rigidity times curvature, for variable rigidity V(s), exact curvature, and arbitrary distributed loads written as double integrals ∫dy∫P ds - ∫dx∫Q ds
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Bernoulli law for the (nonlinear) elastica / Kirchhoff rod equilibrium in the plane
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jacob Bernoulli (1694, constitutive law); Euler (1744 De curvis elasticis, and later general load treatments)
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I; E410 'De gemina methodo...'; E481 'Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flexibilium quam elasticorum' (Novi Comm. 15) — the latter likely the 'alio loco' Euler cites, unsure of exact reference

ideas.what: Curvature formula with no differential taken constant: 1/r = (dy ddx - dx ddy)/ds^3
ideas.modern_name: Signed curvature of a parametrized plane curve
ideas.where_published: Euler's Institutiones calculi differentialis and many mechanics papers

ideas.what: Resultant load integrals ∫P ds, ∫Q ds as the internal force transmitted across the section at Y (completed on the next page with the tension formula)
ideas.modern_name: Internal force resultant / stress resultant of a rod
ideas.where_published: E481 and related papers on flexible and elastic bodies

deep.surprise_reason: This is a restatement, explicitly without proof, of equilibrium equations Euler had already published, including the non-planar extension he mentions. It is standard and well documented in Truesdell's history of rational mechanics of flexible or elastic bodies.
transcription_corrections: Long-s misreadings throughout should be corrected: 'follicitatarum' -> 'sollicitatarum', 'fitas effe affumo' -> 'sitas esse assumo', 'Demonftrationem' -> 'Demonstrationem', 'cafus' -> 'casus', 'elafticae' -> 'elasticae', 'fingulis' -> 'singulis', 'ftatum' -> 'statum', 'maffa' -> 'massa', 'ofculi' -> 'osculi', 'fubftituta' -> 'substituta', 'conftanti' -> 'constanti', 'affumtum' -> 'assumtum', 'refoluantur fecundum' -> 'resoluantur secundum', 'refultans' -> 'resultans', 'pofitis' -> 'positis', 'ftatu' -> 'statu'.
In the image the formulas read correctly as transcribed: V(dy ddx - dx ddy)/ds^3.
